name: fullstack-app
description: Technology-agnostic fullstack application: backend, frontend, domain, persistence, and infrastructure layers with boundary governance
constitution_principles: Domain modules stay free of web frameworks, transport clients, persistence-layer imports, and frontend/UI code.
The backend composes domain logic and persistence through explicit boundaries; business rules do not migrate into route handlers, the frontend, or the persistence layer.
Persistence access is confined to src/db/; backend and domain modules depend on repository or data-access abstractions, never on database drivers or ORM sessions directly.
The frontend communicates with the backend only through the published HTTP/API boundary; it never imports backend, domain, or persistence modules.
Infrastructure-as-code is confined to infra/; application code under src/ never imports infrastructure constructs, and infrastructure code never imports application business logic.
Concrete technology choices (languages, frameworks, datastore, cloud, IaC tool) are recorded per product in an ADR, not fixed by the archetype.
Product code depends on the ObservationProvider abstraction only; observability SDK imports stay inside src/observability/, and the provider is injected at the composition root.

starter_rules.prevents: framework, transport, persistence, or frontend leakage into domain modules
triggers: domain-layer file gains a web framework, transport, persistence, ORM, or frontend/UI import
fullstack plan or implementation collapses domain and backend/persistence boundaries
starter_rules.rule: Keep `src/domain/` framework-independent regardless of the chosen stack. Web frameworks, database clients, ORM sessions, HTTP clients, and frontend/UI libraries belong in `src/backend/`, `src/db/`, or `src/frontend/`, not in domain code.
starter_rules.detection_pattern: Review edits under `src/domain/` for framework, transport, persistence, ORM, or frontend imports (e.g. a web framework such as FastAPI/Express, an ORM such as SQLAlchemy/Prisma, an HTTP client, or a frontend framework such as React/Vue — examples, not an exhaustive allow/deny list).
starter_rules.correct_pattern: Domain modules expose pure business logic. Backend wiring lives in `src/backend/`, persistence in `src/db/`, and frontend code in `src/frontend/`.

starter_rules.prevents: database driver and ORM leakage into backend, domain, or frontend modules
triggers: backend, domain, or frontend file gains a direct database driver or ORM import
raw SQL or ORM session handling appears outside src/db/
starter_rules.rule: Confine database drivers, ORM sessions, and raw queries to `src/db/`, whatever datastore the product selects. Backend and domain modules depend on repository or data-access interfaces exposed by `src/db/`.
starter_rules.detection_pattern: Review edits under `src/backend/`, `src/domain/`, and `src/frontend/` for database driver imports, ORM session creation, or inline SQL.
starter_rules.correct_pattern: `src/db/` exposes repository functions or classes; callers depend on those abstractions and receive them via injection at the composition root.

starter_rules.prevents: the frontend reaching into backend, domain, or persistence internals instead of the API boundary
triggers: frontend file imports from src/backend/, src/domain/, or src/db/
frontend reads or writes persistence directly instead of calling the backend API
starter_rules.rule: Keep `src/frontend/` decoupled from backend internals. The frontend communicates with the backend only through the published HTTP/API boundary; it must not import `src/backend/`, `src/domain/`, or `src/db/`.
starter_rules.detection_pattern: Review imports under `src/frontend/` for relative or package paths into `src/backend/`, `src/domain/`, or `src/db/`.
starter_rules.correct_pattern: The frontend calls backend endpoints over HTTP and depends only on shared, transport-safe contract types (request/response shapes).

starter_rules.prevents: infrastructure-as-code leaking into the application and application logic leaking into infrastructure
triggers: application file under src/ gains an infrastructure-as-code SDK import
infra/ module imports application business logic from src/domain/ or src/backend/
starter_rules.rule: Confine infrastructure-as-code (whatever tool the product selects — CDK, Terraform, Pulumi, etc.) to `infra/`. Application code under `src/` must not import IaC constructs; infrastructure code under `infra/` must not import application business logic.
starter_rules.detection_pattern: Review edits under `src/` for IaC SDK imports (e.g. `aws_cdk`, `pulumi`, `constructs`), and edits under `infra/` for imports of `src.domain` or `src.backend` business modules.
starter_rules.correct_pattern: Infrastructure (compute, networking, secrets) is declared in `infra/`. The application is packaged (e.g. a container image) and deployed by the infra definitions; the two communicate through configuration and environment, not shared imports.
